interactions.title: The monks recognize Delwath
lines: DM: Standing in the doorway as you approach are two old men. Both are wearing loose-fitting white robes. One, a bit younger, is bald; the other is slightly older, with close-cropped gray hair. Both have lined, weathered and deeply tanned faces. As you reach the door, [garbled], they look over you, eyes resting, lingering on Delwath in particular, and the bald one begins to speak, says, I am Pava. This is my companion Avaras. What an unusual crowd to find traveling in the desert. Welcome to our home. Please come in.

DM: Amil, see to their horses and bring us tea when that is done. And he then turns to lead you inside the entryway of of this house to a small sitting area, cushions arranged on the floor, and gestures to you. Please introduce yourselves.

Wellby: Well, Wellby will take off—take off my pack and put down my bow and quiver and sword by the door, and take a seat on one of the cushions and say, Wellby Goodbarrel. Thank you for your hospitality.
Seeker: And I'm Seeker. I keep…
Delwath: Delwath will sort of stay standing, looking at them for a minute, and say, I do not… I mean, I, this is where I don't remember these people at all, right?

DM: No, you don't remember these people at all. You have—you sort of vaguely remember the outskirts of Kharsan and then wandering in the desert, but you're not sure how you got the—the almost 200 miles from Kharsan to Dunmar. You don't have memories of that journey.
Delwath: I am Delwath. I hear from Amil that we might have met before.

DM: That—they sort of look at each other—I'm… And Avaras, who's the—Pava's the bald one; Avaras, with short gray hair—step forward and then just glances back at at Pava and, you know, they seem to be sort of trying to decide something silently, and then turns to you and says…

DM: Indeed, you look… You look better. But— Looks up, looks across at you; you're about the same height. But it is definitely the same face. Less—not so close to death, or so pale. The months have brought you healing, I am glad to see.
DM: It sort of looks back at at Pava. Do you—would you like to to rest? Can we help you with anything? Hey, I'm doing.
Delwath: I am overcome with curiosity as to how you found me, and where I went when I left here.

DM: We did not know where you went. You—you hardly spoke. You—you seemed determined to get away from something, something in the east. And after resting a day and part of a night here, you, you got up and you snuck out, heading west somewhere.

DM: We found you about 20 miles east of here, nearly, nearly dead in the desert, wandering in circles. No food, no water, dying of thirst, muttering something and in, in Elvish, I believe—in some language we do not know. And well, we cannot leave you to die. But you did not seem to want to stay.
Kenzo: Do you remember any of this?
Delwath: Nothing. I recall Kharsan briefly.

DM: You mentioned nothing of Kharsan before. That, that is—that is over 100 miles east of here. Must have traveled quite a distance with no food, no supplies, walking in the desert before we found you. Almost 100 miles.

before: DM: Okay, so, getting us back into Taelgar: five days ago you left Karawa with Havdar and his band of warriors, heading into the desert to investigate the rumors that Alesh had brought back of orcs scouting, gnolls on the move, perhaps other stranger things out east. With Karawa defended by the centaurs and vulnerable refugee population swelling in Tokra, Havdar insisted that a good offense is the best defense, and so with him in the desert you went.

DM: Three days ago you arrived in the ruined town of Bas Udda, a small agricultural village southeast of Karawa, in the shadow of the giant red mesa that looms over the desert here. In Bas Udda you found a young monk, Amil, a Mystai of Bhishma, who had been in town over a week helping the souls of the dead left by the gnoll attack to find peace and rest in the afterlife. After driving off some giant vultures that were angling to snatch some of the decomposing bodies that Amil had recently unearthed, you spoke with him, where you learn that his master's, Pava and Avaras, lived on the edge of the desert in a stone house to the southeast of Bas Udda.

DM: Leaving Havdar's band, you decide to travel with Amil to his masters' house to learn what you could from them. After a questionably unnecessary fight with some ogres just trying to eat some rotting meat in the desert, you continued to this stone house, and as our session begins, you're walking up a rocky slope towards a sprawling, one-story house made of stacked sandstone bricks, homely and incongruous in the dry, barren landscape. The scratching of chickens and the occasional bleat of a goat breaks the silence of the late afternoon sun that's casting a warm glow over the stones of the house.
after: Kenzo: Meta game, can we pull up [garbled]…
Delwath: Map’s on that Roll20.
DM: You're on the map on Roll20.
Kenzo: But the place that he's talking about 100 miles in the desert?
DM: Yeah, that's here.

interactions.title: How the monks survive and serve the dead
lines: Delwath: It's—you're fairly far out from anything here, yes?
DM: We are. That is our way. Have been for many years.
Wellby: How do you keep from getting murdered, like, every week? I mean, we just killed three ogres like an hour ago.

DM: They—they sort of look at each other, and, you know, Pava puts his hand on his head, and Avaras begins to speak it. For many years these lands were quiet. I won't say safe, and certainly not peaceful. More empty than anything else. That has changed. Things are worse. But how do we avoid being murdered? When necessary, we… we vanish.
Kenzo: How do you do that?
DM: Old, old tricks. He taps his foot on the—now you can hear—hollow floor.
DM: Sometimes avoiding conflict is the best we can do to carry out our mission.
DM: And when we were younger, perhaps things were different. But it's been many long years now.
Delwath: Wait, didn't Amil explain some of this to us, right?

DM: Amil explained a little bit, right? That the—so these are like the monks of Bhishma, who was like the matriarchal founder of Dunmar, the country, and they're like mission is to travel across the plague wastes and find people who were never buried, never put to rest, and see that their souls make it to the gods safely. So that's what—that was Amil's purpose in Bas Udda was to basically, cremate the dead, so their souls could rest.

DM: And there were many, many people who died after the Great War, many Dunmari, unmarked and unnoticed in the blasted plains, in the desolation of Cha'mutte, and so this order of monks has take it upon themselves to travel and find those people and see what they can do for them.

before: Kenzo: Kharsan is the name of that, the fortress, then?
DM: The fortress thing, yeah, great. It was once a major Dunmari city.
Wellby: Is it possible, to Wellby, that someone could travel that distance through this terrain and not, like, automatically die on the way?
Unknown: Good question.

DM: Um, I mean, 100 miles would not be easy. It's not completely impossible for a, you know, somebody who's—you know who was probably not a human, but an elf, maybe, right? Somebody who has some, you know, a little bit of a supernatural boost. But you wouldn't—certainly you wouldn't be able to go much further than that and that even 100 miles feels like it would have been unnaturally—I mean, that's difficult in this terrain. You'd have to have had some sense of where you were going, anyway.
after: Seeker: There any plague lands in this area?
DM: Um, not here.
Delwath: What do you know of Kharsan? Middle of the city.
Kenzo: By the way, sorry.

DM: They—they look at each other again. I—And, and sort of look over you, the four of you, and say, We are not untrusting, but I would learn more of your purpose here before we speak too much of the past and our people.

interactions.title: Pava asks the party’s purpose
lines: DM: They—they look at each other again. I—And, and sort of look over you, the four of you, and say, We are not untrusting, but I would learn more of your purpose here before we speak too much of the past and our people.

Kenzo: There are many mysteries we're trying to unravel. Have you seen in the, in the past months, past however long, strange beasts, this commingling and corruption in the nature? Have you seen any evidence of this?

DM: Strange beasts? Yes, there were some that we—well, we know of—we knew of creatures. Seemed more dead than alive, dog-like almost, traveling into the desert, traveling south-west of here. They were not like anything I'd seen since—perhaps since my younger days, anyway.

Kenzo: Do you mind—and I'm assuming a—Seeker doesn't already have his like 3D map, you know of the area—to do you mind if you remember where, where you saw these creatures and when you saw them? We've—they've been attacking and causing tremendous distress in the north of here, as you may have heard word.
Delwath: Mean, these are the same ones we—somebody else told us about these, right? Oh gosh. The gnolls, the half-dead gnolls heading out into the desert.
DM: Yeah, these are these red lines on the map.
Kenzo: Yeah, so they're just confirming what we…
Wellby: Yeah, so what, what is there to the southwest? Is there a abandoned fort, old town, sacred site? If they were going somewhere, where would they be going?
DM: Perhaps the Dustmother. Perhaps you know of her.
Kenzo: What can you tell us about the Dustmother? We believe that the Dustmother is also somehow involved in whatever is going on in the land.
Delwath: Do you know why it's been less quiet?

DM: At this moment, um, Amil walks in with some tea and, and sets it down, serves out iced tea to all of you, and Pava says, A moment, let us—let us take refreshment and hear something of you. I would know what you are doing in the desert. We would— And Avaras jumps in, Yes, we would hear your story before we speak on such topics.

DM: All we know of you is that you are traveling with—God, with, with this elf who... And they both look at each other again, and Avaras sort of nods, and they exchange a look, and Avaras gets up. An elf who did not come to us in the most favorable of circumstances, and left in the night. You've arrived with Amil, which is why we were here to meet you, and he seems to be quite taken with you. But I would hear your something of your story before we continue.

Kenzo: Kenzo is kind of looks over at Pava, in particular, the older bald one and it's just—can—you can tell like Kenzo's kind of entering like a state of like extreme like presence and awareness is just very calmly, you know kind of sitting and…
Kenzo: Looks that—looks at Pava and Avaras.
DM: So Avaras got up and it's gone out of the room with Amil so that's just…

Kenzo: It looks that—looks at Pava. All of our journeys here, I think, had been—you've been brought together by some very strange circumstances. Like Kenzo like laughing generously. I know for myself, I have—I've traveled here as—studying, studying on—studying the lore of the occult, studying on the ways of Laka, Shakun, trying to understand more about other planes of consciousness, about dreams.

Kenzo: I came to this area and Karawa, seeking knowledge, seeking more wisdom and understanding, and when I arrived, just when I first encountered my companions were on—Karawa was being laid siege by these beasts that you described, and we rally to the, to the city. In a way, we've been reacting. We've been—we've been forced to just react to these situations that have been unfolding. We went north to Raven's Hold to search, to try to understand the source of where these beasts came from. We heard word from a variety of sources of different corruption that was spreading across the land. And we've now seen some, I think, really horrible things. There's something very unstable about the land, and not just this Material Plane. Something about the very nature of the fabric of our reality is being impacted, and that is coming from other planes, other dimensions. And we know that Agata Dustmother—we believe—plays a role somehow in what's unfolding. We still don't understand the depths of who is—who or what is behind these disturbances and so, speaking only for myself, I, I know I'm looking for answers, and I think we've been searching together try to understand more.

DM: As you've been talking, he's been sort of staring intently at Kenzo. And he says, You are very strong, young one. You are… Where did you come by these—the sight you have? I have not seen one with your power for many years.
Kenzo: Tim, is Pava—is he, like, a particular branch of the Mystai? Guess you have to, you know…
DM: You don't—I mean, you don't know anything about the Mystai of Bhishma except for…

DM: Possible association is that—oh, that's right, that's you're asking: Bhishma. Bhishma—she's like the matriarch of the Dunmari, and is like the you know the one who collects all the people to her in the afterlife. She's like a demigod. She was…
DM: Honestly, Bhishma is the mother of Shakun, with Laka, who's Shakun's father, right? She's like the you know mortal, okay, partner of Laka.
DM: And then supposedly was you know, became worshiped and acquired some demigod powers after her death.

Kenzo: Anyways, yeah, so, so Kenzo just sort of smiles and thank you for your kind words. I certainly feel very much a novice in the way, but certainly over the past number of years… I'm still trying to unravel and understand my place in this reality be honest. I think each of us is seeking something slightly different along those lines, but this is part of why I travel on here. And perhaps there's much that I am—we—can learn from you.

after: Delwath: Delwath sort of look up in this sort of pause and say, Well, for my part, some—what feels like only a few years ago, me and a number of my people decided that our time of isolation and keeping to ourselves must be over, for elvenkind to make its way in the world. And so we left the forests to fight…
Unknown: And the great evil.

Delwath: And it seems to me that battle is not yet over. And so I have not yet returned home. I am not sure I even know where my home is now. There is much help the younger races need at times. I believe the elves can help and must.

DM: As—as you're speaking, Avaras comes back, and he's, he's carrying something heavy with him, like in a large sack, and he then looks at at Pava. Pava sort of slowly nods, and he's—and then turns to you and says, You say you are—you are, you are—you were fighting against the great evil, Cha'mutte, the shadow dragon. How do you explain this, than?

DM: And Avaras dumps out of this burlap sack a elven breastplate, like your armor from your army days. But there is—shadows sort of collecting and billowing off of that gathering around that. There seems to be some black piece of metal fused to the front of the breastplate, and like as you watch like the shadows seem to coalesce and then like billowing around at. We believe this was yours.

Delwath: It does appear to be mine. I have no memory of it… That is the armor I wore, in a slightly different form, the last battle I fought. Some. Great. We were, we were surrounded by what seemed like 10s of thousands of hobgoblins. Very few of us survived. In the aftermath of that battle I went elsewhere. I cannot explain it.
Kenzo: To us? The implications here are rather terrifying.
Wellby: Wellby looks from one person to another, clearly aware something deep is going on here that he does not understand. This is a—what is this? What are the implications? What are we looking at?
Kenzo: Delwath, do you not remember certain parts of your past because—were you fighting on the wrong side?

Delwath: I think there was very little time I, I lost. No more than a week, perhaps less. I remember the heat of the desert and thirst. I can't remember walking or, or how I made it from place to place.
DM: This, um, so Pava turns and looks at you, and it says this. We do not know how to explain this. It is clearly of elven make.
DM: These shadows do not feel elven.
Delwath: I mean, this is actually…
DM: Literally your armor, you... Yes, and as the…
Delwath: Delwath walk towards it. Yes, this—I recall when this was made. This was made in the years before the Great War, for me. It is my armor. I wore it in the battles—the end of the Great War.
Seeker: But there's been something added to it. I want to find out…

DM: Well, it's not—it's more of that there's like a part—there's like a line down the middle that's been darkened. Like it's all—it's—I don't know, it's been like you know polished steel, right? Nice. It's elven, so it's nice. The work, it's pretty. It probably is designs etched onto it, except that there's this line down the middle that's been darkened, that's just black.
Wellby: Thanks a lot, I found this.

DM: Not—I'm not—not like, like it looks, it looks almost like something was—some other kind of metal was put there and fused to. They did not say where they found that but they seem to assume it's associated with Delwath.
DM: It—He was wearing it when we found him in the desert.
Wellby: Delwath not wearing it now.

DM: We were concerned that the shadows, maybe making him delirious. He seemed… I don't know if contaminated is the right word. Something about these shadows seem connected to him, and I was concerned. So we've removed the armor, and he seems to have left without it.
Delwath: Not all shadows are concerning.
Kenzo: Was your armor always like this, Delwath?
Delwath: Well, this part—pointing at the black thing in the middle—is new. Delwath will walk towards it, and unless they like say…
((Private message logistics and Wellby steps out))

Delwath: So I'm... Delwath will pick up the armor, and as he turns back, he was almost peaceful—or not peaceful exactly, but like accepting. Like, oh, sort of, this is why—he's understood something and—and in his—in his other—he's holding the armor in one hand is his other hand, yeah he sort of—a, a very small like clearly not threatening but a shadow knife appears in his hand and then disappears. But it looks very similar to the darkness, right? The dark thing, like the weapon he summons when he fights, yeah. It's a black shadow long sword, right?
Delwath: And he says, This has been part of me for some time. Is not new.
Delwath: I don't know where… I don't know.
Kenzo: Did you have these abilities before you were in that place?
Delwath: No. But it has not led me astray so far. It's not… Whatever this. Whatever this shadow is that guides my…
Delwath: Powers my weapon—again, like a weapon appears—it is… It is not working against us.

Kenzo: Seeker, do you—can you tell us, do you know where this—when you summon your, your, your abilities, when you bring in your armor, do you know the source of the shadow, you know if it's connected to the Plane of Magic or from someplace else, where it's drawing its energy from?
Kenzo: Seeker, can you, can you divine this?

Seeker: What I can do, Kenzo, let's make an entry into my book of unanswered questions, specifically about this area which we have not yet investigate. It's a good question you're raising, very good question. The thing that I'm a little concerned about is the implication of the connection to Cha'mutte here. That I don't understand.
Delwath: I don't think that—this is definitely not connected to…
Delwath: I guess it feels very different.
Kenzo: When you fought Cha'mutte, you—did you have—you have these abilities?
Delwath: No. They helped me escape the realm I was in. [garbled].

DM: Okay, so I'm back, back in game, um, so, so Pava has been watching, and as he watches Delwath, turns as sort of—him and Avaras nod at each other and they sort of clasp arms for a minute, and says, It does not seem evil. You are right. We were concerned, but your—whatever your… The terror we saw on your face when we found you is gone and has not returned. Is not this armor. It is not the shadows—and did you—are you like putting on the armor? Yeah, so as Delwath is putting on the armor, it seems like he's able to like control the shadows some.
Delwath: No, I'll turn them off if I can. Okay.
DM: Yeah, you can. So the shadows fade and disappear as Delwath puts on the armor.
DM: And I think my concerns are satisfied.

DM: No, there's like a—there's a piece—now that, that you've turned off the shadows, you can see that it's almost like a piece of dark metal that's been subtly embedded in the middle of the breastplate so it's—with the shadows off, now it's clear that it's, it's been done artfully and it doesn't look bad, but it's a different kind of metal. There's some darker metal.
Seeker: It's about eye level to me if we're both standing, right? Yes, it's like awkwardly close, like, What is that, though? If…
Seeker: Clearly, the original manufacture of the armor did not include…
Seeker: This—this type of marking, so it was added later.
Wellby: Is it, um, overlaid, inlaid, or like a film? Does it go all the way through to the backside?
DM: Well, it's a breastplate, right? So it's like you know armor, it's functional armor, it's…
Wellby: All right, so it's not filling in like where the sword that killed Delwath went through his breastplate.
DM: No, Delwath was not killed by a sword. He didn't die. He was alive, so I…

before: Kenzo: I mean, I'm also saying to like, like, this is like potential mentor type of guy, right?
DM: Yeah.
Kenzo: Right, possibly.
Unknown: Interesting, oh.

Kenzo: Anyways, yeah, so, so Kenzo just sort of smiles and thank you for your kind words. I certainly feel very much a novice in the way, but certainly over the past number of years… I'm still trying to unravel and understand my place in this reality be honest. Wellby: But we've no evidence that he isn't.
DM: You come back, Wellby?
Kenzo: Undead shadow elf and a robot.

interactions.title: Agata, the failed ritual, and changing Kharsan
lines: DM: I am willing to speak. I'm willing to answer your questions, if you would ask them. I may have some of my own, for we do not always get news from the west.
Wellby: Well, Wellby just gonna punch right in recklessly, and he'll say, Kenzo said that the magical wall of protection that kept Dunmar shielded has fallen. What can you tell us about that?
DM: That is grave news. I can tell you nothing of the cause. Is this…
Kenzo: We wonder if the Dustmother's involved. What can you tell us of the Dustmother?
DM: She is… How to describe her? We try to avoid that area. Those who die in her clutches rarely have souls left to save to begin with. She is—she is misery incarnate.

DM: Does not seem like something she would do, though, to… She has never sought conquest or territory. She has sought to make everybody's lives just a little bit worse. But we are not experts in the workings of such creatures, and maybe something has changed. Maybe she, she made a bargain. Maybe there was something she wanted enough.
Seeker: We've heard tell that she wants revenge, vengeance for the defeat of allies in the Great War.
DM: That could be. I mean, we always thought she was just evil. But maybe her cruelty is driven by a desire for revenge. It's possible.
Seeker: But who might she have made a bargain with? Who's in a position to do her a favor?

DM: As we said... And they sort of again look over each other, their... Things have been bad over the past year. And has been... We came here. And Avaras sort of picks up the story here. We came here in—30, more than 30 years ago now. We wanted a quiet life. Helping souls find their way, yes, but not bothered by the troubles of politics and war. And it might seem like moving to the blasted plains, the desolation, what people call the desolation of Cha'mutte, would not be a place you move for a quiet life. But look around—and was—nothing can live here. There was nothing here. Agata Dustmother, yes, but honestly, she keeps to herself unless you seek her out. Or had.

DM: And about 30 years ago, many in our order, but before we were even masters, when we were wanderers in the desert, but just before we had settled here and we're, you know, achieved the status—something happened. Many in our order died. There was a—a plan, some attempt to cleanse the land. There was somebody who, you know, one of the leaders… Don't know the details. It was a secret. Some way to remove the curse that lies over this place, but it did not work, it was... And after that, even more so, we wanted quiet. We wanted somewhere just to avoid the dangers and the troubles of the world and tend to the souls of those who had passed on, as was our calling.

DM: And for almost all of the past 30 years, it has been that life. Few passed by here. We travel as we need. We've taken some apprentices who have gone on to be wanderers themselves and traveled through the desert. But soon before we found you, Delwath, something changed and Pava picks up the story here.

DM: Don't know what it was that changed exactly, but something happened in Kharsan. It's always been a haunted place. It's always been a place where one does not travel because of the nightmare—nightmares of the mists, the killing mists of the plague years. But it's never been a place that felt like there was an evil will at work behind. That changed.

DM: There's the orcs that live out east in the desert. For many years they seemed to live quietly on their own. Not what I would expect of orcs, but such was their way, living in the desert. In the past year that has changed. They've been fighting each other, some coming west. Even twice now we've had to hide from orcs.

Wellby: But we've no evidence that he isn't.

Kenzo: Undead shadow elf and a robot.
Unknown: So…
after: DM: The—and not six—no, maybe two months ago, a month ago—more adventurers. DM: We were suspicious and did not speak to them, but listened from a distance. I do not believe they were aware of us, and they have not returned. You saw there were five of them, you saw that.

Unknown: East.
